\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পরিসংখ্যান} (pôrisôngkhyān)}{পরিসংখ্যান (pôrisôngkhyān)}]{\bn{পরিসংখ্যান} (pôrisôngkhyān) — statistics}

\label{lesson:BN-C355-porisongkhyan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to discover, then the Bengali for to look into.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পরিসংখ্যান}}
\textbf{\bn{পরিসংখ্যান}} — \emph{pôrisôngkhyān} — \textquotedblleft{}statistics\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{পরিসংখ্যানটা} \bn{আমাকে} \bn{দেখাও।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pôrisôngkhyānṭā āmāke dekhāo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Show me the statistics.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পরিসংখ্যান}} (\emph{pôrisôngkhyān}) is Sanskrit \emph{parisaṃkhyāna}, a full count (Monier-Williams). Modern Bengali uses it for statistics.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôrisôngkhyān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôrisôngkhyān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôrisôngkhyānṭā āmāke dekhāo.} — Show me the statistics.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to discover, then the Bengali for to look into, then say \emph{pôrisôngkhyān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{পরিসংখ্যান} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Statistics\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{নমুনা} (nômunā)}{নমুনা (nômunā)}]{\bn{নমুনা} (nômunā) — a sample; a specimen}

\label{lesson:BN-C355-nomuna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to look into, then the Bengali for statistics.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{নমুনা}}
\textbf{\bn{নমুনা}} — \emph{nômunā} — \textquotedblleft{}a sample; a specimen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ডাক্তার} \bn{রক্তের} \bn{নমুনা} \bn{নিলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḍāktār rôkter nômunā nilen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor took a blood sample.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{নমুনা}} (\emph{nômunā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{namūna}, a pattern or sample: a small part that shows what the whole is like.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nômunā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍāktār rôkter nômunā nilen.} — The doctor took a blood sample.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to look into, then the Bengali for statistics, then say \emph{nômunā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{জরিপ} (jôrip)}{জরিপ (jôrip)}]{\bn{জরিপ} (jôrip) — a survey}

\label{lesson:BN-C355-jorip}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for statistics, then the Bengali for a sample.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{জরিপ}}
\textbf{\bn{জরিপ}} — \emph{jôrip} — \textquotedblleft{}a survey\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমরা} \bn{পাড়ায়} \bn{একটা} \bn{জরিপ} \bn{করলাম।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmrā pāṛāy ekṭā jôrip kôrlām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We carried out a survey in the neighbourhood.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{জরিপ}} (\emph{jôrip}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{jarīb}, a measure of land, through Persian; it first meant a land survey and then any survey.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôrip}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôrip}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmrā pāṛāy ekṭā jôrip kôrlām.} — We carried out a survey in the neighbourhood.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for statistics, then the Bengali for a sample, then say \emph{jôrip} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সংগ্রহ} \bn{করা} (sônggrôhô kôrā)}{সংগ্রহ করা (sônggrôhô kôrā)}]{\bn{সংগ্রহ} \bn{করা} (sônggrôhô kôrā) — to collect; to gather (data, money)}

\label{lesson:BN-C355-songgroho-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a sample, then the Bengali for a survey.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সংগ্রহ} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{সংগ্রহ} \bn{করা}} — \emph{sônggrôhô kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to collect; to gather (data, money)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ছাত্ররা} \bn{গ্রাম} \bn{থেকে} \bn{তথ্য} \bn{সংগ্রহ} \bn{করল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chhātrôrā grām theke tôthyô sônggrôhô kôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The students collected information from the village.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{অনেক} \bn{পুরনো} \bn{বই} \bn{সংগ্রহ} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini ônek purôno bôi sônggrôhô kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সংগ্রহ} \bn{করা}} (\emph{sônggrôhô kôrā}) is Sanskrit \emph{saṃgraha}, collecting or gathering together (Monier-Williams), with \bn{করা}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chhātrôrā grām theke tôthyô sônggrôhô kôrlô.} — The students collected information from the village.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a sample, then the Bengali for a survey, then say \emph{sônggrôhô kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বিশ্লেষণ} \bn{করা} (bishleshôn kôrā)}{বিশ্লেষণ করা (bishleshôn kôrā)}]{\bn{বিশ্লেষণ} \bn{করা} (bishleshôn kôrā) — to analyse}

\label{lesson:BN-C355-bishleshon-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a survey, then the Bengali for to collect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বিশ্লেষণ} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{বিশ্লেষণ} \bn{করা}} — \emph{bishleshôn kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to analyse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বিজ্ঞানীরা} \bn{নমুনাগুলো} \bn{বিশ্লেষণ} \bn{করলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bigyānīrā nômunāgulo bishleshôn kôrlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The scientists analysed the samples.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{ফলাফল} \bn{বিশ্লেষণ} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini phôlāphôl bishleshôn kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বিশ্লেষণ} \bn{করা}} (\emph{bishleshôn kôrā}) is Sanskrit \emph{viśleṣaṇa}, separating (Monier-Williams), with \bn{করা}. 'To analyse', taking a thing apart to study it, is the modern sense.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bishleshôn kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bishleshôn kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bigyānīrā nômunāgulo bishleshôn kôrlen.} — The scientists analysed the samples.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a survey, then the Bengali for to collect, then say \emph{bishleshôn kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বিশ্লেষণ} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To analyse\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
